messages:
Alex: Heads up — customer asked if we can apply their cloud commitment (3yr reserved credits) when Redwood manages their Private VPC. They want line-item pricing that reflects the lower unit cost.

Maria: Short answer: only if the VPC stays in the customer's cloud account. If we run infra in our account, their commitment doesn't attach.

Kevin: Technical twist: our billing currently attributes infra as Redwood spend when instances are in our accounts. To honor a customer CUD directly we'd need them to retain those resources in their account or set up some marketplace resale arrangement (rare).

Raj: Sales note: some enterprise buyers expect an invoice that looks like "GPU infra (pass-through)" and then a separate software license. They often don't care who pays cloud infra as long as net price meets procurement targets.

Sasha: Legal/tax reminder: even if we show a pass-through line, taxability depends on jurisdiction. Many APAC/EU authorities treat pass-through as taxable revenue unless we have proper supporting receipts. Also, if we accept their commitment into our account, contractually the cloud provider will not let us transfer it.

Alex: Could we do a middle ground — Redwood manages infra but applies a monthly rebate that mirrors their committed unit price?

Maria: That's viable commercially. We can offer a $/GPU-hr credit in the contract that is reconciled monthly against usage, contingent on the customer providing monthly cloud usage exports for audit. Finance prefers fixed per-unit credits for simplicity.

Kevin: Implementation gaps I anticipate: our meter currently emits {instance, region, gpu_count, hours}. To apply customer-specific credits we need: (1) customer_id on meter lines, (2) region-aware mapping, (3) ability to apply negative line items with supporting reference to cloud invoice. We also need to record which hours are covered by the commitment band vs burst.

Raj: Example invoice mockup for the "rebate" pattern:
```
1) Redwood infra (gross): g5.4xlarge | us-east-1 | 4 GPUs | 720h | $1.60/hr | $1,152.00
2) Commitment credit: Customer X committed price offset | 720h | -$0.45/hr | -$324.00
3) Redwood software license: Private deployment | monthly | $5,000.00
Total due: $5,828.00
```

Sasha: Requirements if we do credits: contract language explicitly ties credits to verifiable usage exports, credits expire with term, no third-party transfer of cloud commitments implied. Also include audit right for 12 months.

Maria: Ops/region nuance: credits should be regionalized or expressed per-region because GPU list prices differ widely (e.g., eu-west-1 vs us-west-2). Finance can publish a region rate table for credits.

Alex: Any precedent we can point to?

Kevin: Pilot last year with "NordTech" — we managed burst infra, NordTech kept base in their account. We issued monthly credits for the burst only, tied to a fixed $/GPU-hr. We did not take ownership of their reserved commitment.

Raj: From a sales perspective, present 3 options to customers:
- Option A (best for customer): Customer keeps base infra in their account; Redwood invoices SW only, we handle integration.
- Option B (managed + credit): Redwood manages infra, customer gets monthly credit based on agreed $/GPU-hr and usage reports.
- Option C (hybrid): Customer-managed baseline + Redwood-managed burst; clear delimiting of what is credited.

Alex: Action items:
- Maria: draft 2 invoice templates (Option A & B) and sample contract clauses for credits (EOD Thu)
- Kevin: list required billing/metering fields and estimated engineering effort to support customer credits (Wed)
- Sasha: short legal memo on tax/audit implications and recommended clause language (Thu)
- Raj: collect 3 active deals asking for this and drop procurement counters from customers (Mon)

Maria: I'll add region rate table draft to the invoice templates. Also recommend a minimum commit band to justify monthly reconciliation overhead (e.g., >$10k/mo infra).

Kevin: FYI: monitoring-wise, we should also expose a "committed usage" dashboard so customers can see how much of their CUD-equivalent they're consuming when hybrid. That makes audits smoother.

billing-bot: Draft invoice uploaded: https://files.redwood/invoices/drafts/rdw-credit-pattern-example.pdf (uploaded by Maria)

Alex: Good discussion. We'll reconvene once docs and tech gap list are in. :thumbsup:
